Perfect-foresight preserves positive value for price-responsive, within-session EVMC applied to up to 45% of the LDV fleet. Within-week per-vehicle production cost savings are maximized by RTP at low participation rates, but TOU and RTP production cost savings are low or negative with 45% of the LDV fleet actively scheduling weekly charging because it becomes difficult to serve electricity demand from all the EVs trying to charge in the lowest-cost hours. 3.2 The Value of Perfect-foresight Compared to No-foresight Foresight value is higher at higher participation rates, for within-week compared to within-session flexibility, and for RTP compared to TOU. The additional value unlocked by accurately forecasting EV load increases as more EV charging is managed and managed more flexibly. Figure 3 directly compares no-foresight (day-ahead unit commitment based on unmanaged EV profiles) and perfect-foresight (day-ahead unit commitment based on actual EV profiles, after price-responsive vehicles respond to RTP or TOU prices) annual per-vehicle production cost savings, with negative production cost savings truncated at zero to preserve y-axis legibility. The gaps between perfect-foresight and no- foresight savings, which are always positive and we refer to as foresight value, are largest for RTP with within-week flexibility. As shown in Table A.2, foresight value ranges from $10/vehicle-yr (2% of LDVs responding to TOU) to $1,052/vehicle-yr (27% of LDVs responding to RTP) for within-week flexibility. For within-session flexibility, we observe lower foresight value, ranging from $5/vehicle-yr (2% of LDVs responding to RTP) to $284/vehicle-yr (45% of LDVs responding to RTP). In both cases, foresight value exceeds perfect-foresight production cost savings at moderate participation shares (by 27% of LDVs for within-session flexibility and by 14% of LDVs for within-week flexibility) and continues growing as 12 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. participation shares increase. Because perfect-foresight production cost savings decline with increasing participation shares, this trend implies the effectiveness of price-responsive dispatch mechanisms becomes more dependent on accurate day-ahead forecasts of actual response as participation rates grow.
